title: Observability and the output rank test

sections.heading: The idea

sections.body_md:
Observability asks whether the sensor can see every state. If a finite record of \(y\) determines \(x(0)\), the pair is observable. The test stacks the output row \(C\) on top of \(CA\), \(CA^2\), and so on. Full rank means the only state that produces zero output for all time is the zero state. A short rank means a hidden mode: an eigenvalue of \(A\) that never reaches the measurement.

This is the dual of reachability. The input test stacks columns \(B, AB, \ldots\). The output test stacks rows. A coordinate change preserves the rank, just as it preserves reachability.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
For \(n\) states,
\[
\mathcal{O} = \begin{bmatrix} C \\ CA \\ \vdots \\ CA^{n-1} \end{bmatrix}.
\]
The pair is observable when \(\mathrm{rank}\,\mathcal{O} = n\). Equivalently, \((A^T, C^T)\) passes the reachability rank test. In observable canonical form the stacked matrix is triangular. A cancelled factor in a transfer function is a mode that is hidden or unreachable, so a minimal realization has dropped it.

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: Let \(A = \mathrm{diag}(-0.35, -1.7)\) and \(C = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 6 \end{bmatrix}\). Then \(CA = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -10.2 \end{bmatrix}\). Both rows have a zero in the first column, so the mode at \(-0.35\) produces no output and no derivative of the output. That column is a hidden direction. Changing the sensor to \(C = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 6 \end{bmatrix}\) fills the column, and every mode then reaches the measurement.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md: A nonzero \(C\) is not a full test. Two proportional rows still have rank 1. The dual uses the transpose: \((A^T, C^T)\), not \((C, A)\) with the factors merely swapped. A hidden mode need not be unstable. It is simply absent from \(y\), which is why a transfer function can have lower degree than the state matrix you started with. And the canonical form is full rank only when nothing was cancelled.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: An observer copies the model and corrects it with a gain times \(y - C\hat{x}\). That gain can put the error eigenvalues anywhere you like only when the pair is observable. A hidden mode stays where \(A\) put it, and no choice of the gain will move it. Designing the gain is the next skill.
